The configuration described is a classic one: the internal bisector of \(\angle BAC\) meets the circumcircle of \(\triangle ABC\) at the midpoint \(M\) of the arc \(BC\) that does **not** contain \(A\).  

For any triangle,
\[
\begin{aligned}
\text{circumradius } R &= \frac{a}{2\sin A},\qquad a=BC,\\
AM &= 2R\sin A = a .
\end{aligned}
\]
Hence the length \(AM\) is exactly the side \(BC\), i.e. \(AM = 7\).

The proposed solution arrived at \(AM = \dfrac{9}{2}\) by an unjustified “harmonic/arithmetic” argument and does not satisfy the invariant \(AM = BC\). Therefore the final answer is incorrect.
